title: Token velocity throttler with adaptive credit restitution
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We observe short, high-frequency bursts from a small set of tenants that cause disproportionate token consumption and transient billing anomalies in the Console. These bursts trigger emergency throttles, cascade through the KV cache and batching layers, and produce late-arrival tokens that our ledger reconciliation job finds difficult to attribute cleanly. Goal: Implement a lightweight per-tenant token velocity throttler that enforces soft-burst limits, integrates with the existing credit pool allocator, and has an adaptive restitution mechanism to return unused reserved credits in the face of request cancellations and late-arriving meter events. This should reduce 'spiky' billing noise, lower emergency throttle incidents, and improve the quality of downstream billing attribution (fewer retro credits/adjustments).
acceptance_criteria: Soft-burst throttle enforces configured tokens/sec and tokens/min per-tenant without causing >5% additional median latency for normal requests
Unused reserved credits are restituted back to tenant pool within configured window (default 2 minutes) for >95% of cancellations/aborts
Late-arrival tokens (arriving >30s after initial request) are reconciled and tagged with provenance so billing reconciler can correctly attribute without manual adjustments
End-to-end test harness and simulation show 40% reduction in emergency throttle invocations for synthetic bursty workload
Monitoring dashboards (Console) show per-tenant throttle events, restitution metrics, and reconciliation status
implementation_notes: Architecture: lightweight token-velocity controller as a set of pods in console-backend that subscribes to a tenant-config topic and maintains in-memory windows (sliding) for velocity enforcement

Coordinator: use Redis (primary) with Kafka fanout for cross-region eventing; Redis stores ephemeral reservations and restitution tombstones; Kafka ensures subscribers converge for multi-region dedicated clusters

Accounting: on request start, reserve from a tenant soft-pool; on completion or cancel, emit a restitution event. Restitution worker consumes events and performs idempotent add-back to pool and emits a provenance-tagged ledger correction if necessary

Idempotency & late-arrival: attach trace id + provisional token id to meter events; reconciliation job will match by provisional id. If unmatched within restitution window, create a compensating ledger item with note 'late-arrival-unmatched'

Backpressure strategy: when tenant is over soft-burst, we return 429 with 'retry-after' and a structured reason for client SDKs to surface. For high-priority customers we route to emergency burst queue (configurable per-tenant)
tradeoffs: Redis + Kafka increases operational surface vs purely in-db approach, but provides lower tail latency and better cross-region propagation for Dedicated deployments
Using soft-burst + restitution will still allow short penalty for violated SLA, but prevents persistent punitive throttles that cause long-running reconciliation churn
Complexity of provisional IDs adds matching work in reconciler but materially reduces false-positive retro credits
